question: Due to an error, a shopkeeper increases the selling price of a Rs 500 item by 10% instead of decreasing it by 10%. What is the percentage increase in the price due to this error?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The base price of ₹500 is not needed to find the percentage error; use 100% directly.

Intended SP = 100% − 10% = 90%

Erroneous SP = 100% + 10% = 110%

Percentage Error = [(Erroneous SP − Intended SP) ÷ Intended SP] × 100

= [(110 − 90) ÷ 90] × 100 = 200 ÷ 9 = 22.22%

**∴ The correct answer is 22.22%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Original Price = ₹500

Intended price change = Decrease by 10%

Erroneous price change = Increase by 10%

**Formula Used:**

Percentage Increase = (Increase in Value ÷ Original Correct Value) × 100

 Price Error Comparison
 
 Original
 
 ₹500
 
 Intended SP
 
 ₹450 (−10%)
 
 Erroneous SP
 
 ₹550 (+10%)

 
• 
 
• 
 

 Gap = ₹100
 
 Error % = (100 ÷ 450) × 100 = 22.22%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Intended correct price = 500 − (10% of 500) = 500 − 50 = ₹450

⇒ Erroneous actual price = 500 + (10% of 500) = 500 + 50 = ₹550

⇒ Price increase due to error = 550 − 450 = ₹100

⇒ Percentage increase = (100 ÷ 450) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = 1000 ÷ 45 = 200 ÷ 9 ≈ 22.22%

**∴ The correct answer is 22.22%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Error Base Requirement

Percentage error must always be calculated with respect to the true (intended) value acting as the base denominator. Formula: (|True Value − Actual Value| ÷ True Value) × 100.

Base Independence Trick

When both the intended change and the erroneous change are provided as percentages, the final error percentage is entirely independent of the original numerical value (like ₹500). Solving logically with an assumed base of 100 prevents unnecessary calculations.

Percentage Increase / Decrease Concept

A numerical value increased by x% effectively becomes Value × (1 + x/100). Similarly, a value decreased by x% mathematically becomes Value × (1 − x/100).
